routes.approach: Separate the finite group lemmas from evaluation. Write a=(01) and s=(02) in the endpoint’s zero-based Fin 3. Show the first-factor subgroup contains just 1 and a by involutivity. Classify a permutation by whether it fixes 2. The permutations fixing 2 lie in this subgroup; the remaining four are s, a*s, s*a, a*s*a. Prove this on the three point values by finite cases and permutation extensionality, without normalizing the diagram. The entire C₂ factor is in K, so DoubleCoset.eq yields exactly the two classes and their distinctness. Conjugation by s transports a to (21); the two first-factor involutions are distinct, so the two Mackey subgroups are K and L. Deduce their intersection is L, and use the source's centrality computation to reconcile the right embeddings with conjugators 1 and s⁻¹. L and K have cardinalities 2 and 4; use relIndex_mul_card to get the two reviewed indices. For evaluation instantiate CommonMackeyIntersectionSum at α=β=1, G=⊤ and the selection of both class representatives. Transfer the classifier via Subgroup.topEquiv so this supplier's ranges and MackeyIdentityDiagram's comaps describe the same quotient. Construct the prescribed two-valued section and compare the corresponding conjugation embeddings and dot elements. The common subgroup from the supplier is exactly L. Normalize its two restricted columns, then use MackeyIdentityDiagram for the identity of the full outer sum. At x, enlarge support to these two indices since outside the support every term is zero. Reindex only evaluations and check the reviewed drawing keeps the binary plus explicitly drawn in Example 5.1, with scale 1/2 on the first complete stack and the second complete stack unscaled. Coefficient 1 agrees after evaluation. The two standalone cup conditions are available here from the finite groups if using the finite-cup branch; the reviewed compact diagrams can use the finite mixed-fiber branch directly. Right conjugation maps agree with the reference iff every σ j₀·(σ j)⁻¹ centralizes the subgroup; then all pairwise equalities follow. Hence admissible S is precisely parabolic S with S ≤ P in the reviewed definition. Prove G finite by restricting its block permutations to the union of its finite support blocks, then P finite by inclusion. Map P to Equiv.Perm Nat by the finitary inclusion. Apply ExtremalParabolicsOfFiniteGroup there and transport its greatest property back along the inclusion. Use MonoidHom.map_closure and injectivity, check swap membership in both directions, and match its parabolic predicate by taking the union of the finite partition blocks. Nonzero finite relative indices supply the monotonicity and the nonzero Complex denominators. For each j in the selected subtype use the newly compiled CommonMackeyIntersectionSum's arbitrary-S first conjunct with S equal to the constructed swap closure, or the direct MixedCrossingsThroughSmallerGroup theorem. This arbitrary-subgroup clause supplies both fiber certificates and the ordinary per-term normalization. Its separate selected-family normalization fixes S to the full intersection and can apply only if that subgroup agrees with this hull. Rewrite the ordinary comparisons to the exact coefficient-one labelled stacks with the compact adapters.
